title: All common non-increasing VPD weights kept heated ozone summaries no higher in North Wales in August-September 2021
abstract: We tested whether dry-air weighting can reverse heated-minus-ambient ozone summaries in a North Wales wildflower experiment. We used 1,464 complete hourly records in August and September 2021 and three paired ozone targets. An exact cumulative-sum test gave sharp bounds over all common non-increasing vapor pressure deficit weights from zero to one. None of 48 month, target, light-rule and ozone-threshold combinations allowed a positive contrast. With light above 50 micromoles per square metre per second, six unweighted contrasts were -4.77 to -0.73 ppb. Their lower bounds were -37.14 to -13.92 ppb and all upper bounds were zero. Independent linear programs confirmed all bounds. These are conditional exposure summaries, not ozone uptake or causal effects on flowers. One site-year, one chamber per treatment, shared ambient weather, possible source filling and an untested common response limit inference. Independent regions and years remain untested. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, retrieval instructions and a figure support reproduction.

display.caption: Cumulative signed ozone sums give sharp bounds for every common non-increasing VPD weight. Each panel shows one month and target pair. No cumulative sum is positive. The orange line is the unweighted contrast. This is an exposure diagnostic, not an uptake model.
